root.name: Benoni Defense: Uhlmann Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 c5 4. d5 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. Nc3 g6 7. Bg5

overview: In the Benoni, White develops 7.Bg5 and after 7...Bg7 plays 8.e4 h6 9.Bh4 g5 10.Bg3 Nh5, or 7...h6. White has a space edge and the d5 wedge, while Black plays for ...b5 and ...Nbd7 and counterplay on the e-file and queenside. The game is double-edged.

white_ideas.idea: Push e4 and e5 with space
Pin and attack Black knight with Bg5, Qd2

typical_structures.structure: Benoni pawn structure: White d5/e4, Black c5/d6

character.notes: After 8.e4 h6 9.Bh4 g5 both sides take real risks: White pushes e5 or Nd2 with space, Black counters on the e-file and queenside.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: A respected main line where Black has an accepted way to equalise.

structure.notes: Asymmetric Benoni centre, White d5/e4 against Black c5/d6, with Black half-open e- and b-files.

approach.notes: A standard sideline against the Benoni, in the repertoire of strong players on both sides.

level.notes: Needs concrete move-order knowledge and the e5 and ...b5 plans.

character.reason: Double-edged play where one slip loses quickly.

soundness.reason: A recognised line for both sides.

structure.reason: Fixed asymmetric centre with files to press on, though it can read as closed.

approach.reason: A main sideline of the Benoni.

plans.reason: White space in the centre, Black queenside play.
